releases.name: v0.3.3 — Tested with OpenCode 2.2.4, used-up limits stop at once
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.3.3

This release moves the tested host to OpenCode 2.2.4, stops at once when a
model's usage or spend limit is used up, and shows the OpenCode version in
`/pr-check` instead of a notice on every receipt. Reviews, comment previews,
adjustments and publication work as in 0.3.2.

## What changed

- **Tested with OpenCode 2.2.4.** AZPR is validated with OpenCode CLI 2.2.4
  instead of 2.1.4. The runtime needed no change: with the same fake provider,
  a review sends byte-identical model requests on both hosts. OpenCode 2.2.x
  offers new tools to every agent, such as image generation when a provider has
  an image model; private reviewers still see only AZPR's tools and the native
  read tools.
- **OpenCode version in `/pr-check`.** A new OpenCode row names the host
  version and is a WARNING when it is not the tested one; reviews still run,
  and AZPR still refuses to start if OpenCode lacks something it needs.
  Receipts no longer end with a host notice after every OpenCode update.
- **Used-up limits stop at once.** When a model's usage or spend limit is used
  up, AZPR refuses OpenCode's retries, starts no new session, and the receipt
  names the limit. Besides the provider quota and the OpenCode free-model
  limit, this covers the ChatGPT and OpenCode Go usage limits that OpenCode
  2.2.3 reports and OpenCode's spend limits; a used-up ChatGPT limit was
  previously retried as a rate limit.
- **Fewer host events.** AZPR subscribes only to the session events that show
  a review progressing; OpenCode 2.2.0 and later deliver no others.
- **Proxies.** OpenCode 2.2.4 always adds `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` and `::1`
  to `NO_PROXY`, and Bun honours `NO_PROXY` even for `azure.proxy`. Azure
  DevOps requests are unaffected; the
  [company-network guide](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.3.3/docs/ENTERPRISE.md#company-networks)
  now says to keep `dev.azure.com` out of `NO_PROXY` when it must use the
  proxy.

## Upgrading OpenCode

OpenCode 2.2.0 and later migrate OpenCode's database when they first start,
and the migration cannot be undone. Stop the service and back up the database
before installing 2.2.4:

```sh
opencode service stop
mkdir -p ~/opencode-db-backup && cp -p ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db* ~/opencode-db-backup/
npm install -g @opencode/cli@2.2.4
opencode service start
```

Use `sudo` for the global install if your npm prefix needs it. To go back,
stop the service, reinstall the previous OpenCode and restore the backup.
AZPR 0.3.3 also runs on OpenCode 2.1.4 (`/pr-check` then shows the OpenCode
WARNING row), so the two upgrades can happen in either order.

## Installation

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.3.3
```

Alternatively, install the same release from Git:

```sh
opencode plugin add 'github:WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2#v0.3.3'
```

Add only one of them. Follow the
[quickstart](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.3.3/docs/QUICKSTART.md)
for a private PAT file, `/pr-setup`, a service restart and the first review.

## Upgrading AZPR

For an entry that `opencode plugin add` created, add 0.3.3 and remove the
previous version only when the download succeeded. Replace `PREVIOUS_VERSION`
with the version in your `plugins` entry, such as 0.3.2:

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.3.3 &&
  opencode plugin remove opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@PREVIOUS_VERSION
```

Run them when no AZPR command is running: OpenCode 2.1.4 and 2.2.4 switch the
running service to 0.3.3 within seconds, without a restart, and
`opencode plugin list` should then show a single `azpr` row with 0.3.3. Running
only the first command leaves the previous version running. For an entry with
options, change only its `package` value; the OpenCode service then downloads
0.3.3 with its own network settings. See
[upgrading](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2

releases.name: v0.3.2 — Results first, precise receipts, smaller npm package
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.3.2

This release shows AZPR's actual Azure DevOps output at the top of the README,
states the COMPLETE status more precisely in receipts, and slims the npm
package to the runtime. Reviews, comment previews, adjustments and publication
work as in 0.3.1.

## What changed

- **See the output first.** The README opens with an actual inline comment on
  a dedicated test PR, shown with its code context, and the complete PR summary
  from the same review. The first-review steps follow, then the 15-second
  recording of adjusting findings and publishing. The
  [demo](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.3.2/docs/DEMO.md#actual-azure-devops-comments)
  records the capture run and its editing, and lists the pictured comments as
  text.
- **Precise status.** COMPLETE in a receipt now means that no source-commit
  change was detected. When the final version recheck itself fails, the review
  stays COMPLETE and its report lists a warning; publication still rechecks
  that the PR is active and its source commit is unchanged before posting.
- **Smaller npm package.** The package holds the runtime (`server.js` and
  `src/`), the README, the changelog and the license: 32 files and about 170 KB
  instead of 76 files and 1.35 MB. Documentation, media, installers and the
  settings example and schema remain in the repository and the source archive,
  and npmjs.com shows the README's links and images from GitHub.
- **Documentation.** The README and the architecture guide list the commands
  that answer directly instead of starting a background run, and the README
  and the commenting guide state that repeating the saved adjustments plans
  nothing.

## Installation

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.3.2
```

Alternatively, install the same release from Git:

```sh
opencode plugin add 'github:WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2#v0.3.2'
```

Add only one of them. Follow the
[quickstart](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.3.2/docs/QUICKSTART.md)
for a private PAT file, `/pr-setup`, a service restart and the first review.

## Upgrading

For an entry that `opencode plugin add` created, add 0.3.2 and remove the
previous version only when the download succeeded. Replace `PREVIOUS_VERSION`
with the version in your `plugins` entry, such as 0.3.1:

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.3.2 &&
  opencode plugin remove opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@PREVIOUS_VERSION
```

Run them when no AZPR command is running: OpenCode 2.1.4 switches the running
service to 0.3.2 within seconds, without a restart, and `opencode plugin list`
should then show a single `azpr` row with 0.3.2. Running only the first command
leaves the previous version running. For an entry with options, change only
its `package` value; the OpenCode service then downloads 0.3.2 with its own
network settings. See
[upgrading](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.3.2/README.md#upgrading)
for the details. External settings, the PAT file and review records remain in
place, and this release adds no settings or required migration.

For a source installation, extract the new archive and run its installer with
`--replace` to retain settings:

```sh
sh install.sh --config-dir /absolute/path/to/v2-opencode-config --replace
```

## Compatibility and validation

The tested target remains OpenCode CLI **2.1.4** (V2 plugin API), Node.js
**22.23.3**, Ubuntu **22.04.5** under WSL2, and Azure DevOps Services REST API
**7.1**. OpenCode 1.x and Azure DevOps Server are not supported; other operating
systems remain unvalidated.

describes the release checks with fake services. The runtime changes only the

releases.name: v0.3.1 — Easier installation, setup and upgrades
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.3.1

This release makes installation, first-run setup and upgrades easier to
follow on OpenCode 2.1.4, and lets `/pr-check` show which AZPR is running.
Reviews, comment previews, adjustments and publication work as in 0.3.0.

## What changed

- **Shorter setup.** `/pr-setup --organization YOUR_ORGANIZATION --model
  PROVIDER/MODEL` uses the PAT file the quickstart creates,
  `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/azpr/pat`, and `--organization` also accepts
  your PR's URL. With `--replace`, setup keeps the PAT file already set unless
  you name another one. The receipt names the organization and the PAT file.
- **See what runs.** `/pr-check` has an **AZPR** row that names the running
  package and version. When another AZPR entry is configured but not running,
  for example after `opencode plugin add` with a new version, which leaves the
  old one running, the row is a WARNING. User names, passwords and query
  strings in package specifications are masked.
- **Restart only for settings.** On OpenCode 2.1.4, adding or changing the
  plugin entry loads it into the running service within seconds. Saved
  settings still need a restart, and AZPR's messages now name
  `opencode service restart`.
- **Documentation.** The quickstart runs the terminal steps first. The README
  has an Upgrading section. The team guide explains proxies and certificates
  for package downloads, model providers and Azure DevOps separately, and the
  Azure DevOps guide names the actual settings locations.

## Installation

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.3.1
```

Alternatively, install the same release from Git:

```sh
opencode plugin add 'github:WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2#v0.3.1'
```

leaves the previous version running. For an entry with options, change only
its `package` value; the OpenCode service then downloads 0.3.1 with its own
network settings. See
[upgrading](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.3.1/README.md#upgrading)

releases.name: v0.3.0 — Adjust findings before publishing
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.3.0

AI reviews. You decide what gets posted. This release lets you exclude findings
or change their severity after reading a comment preview. AZPR prepares a new
preview without rerunning the review, while keeping the original findings and
report intact.

## Try it after a preview

Use your review ID and finding IDs from its report:

```text
/pr-comment <review-id> --exclude F-1 --severity F-2=low
```

F-1 is excluded from the new preview; F-2 appears as low in the summary, with no
new inline comment. Comment planning uses a model again, so other wording may
change. Read the whole new preview, then publish from the same conversation:

```text
/pr-comment <review-id> --publish
```

## What changed

- **Choose the findings and severity.** `--exclude` and `--severity` each
  replace their own saved list; `none` empties that list. For example,
  `--exclude F-1` followed by `--exclude F-2` excludes only F-2. Name both to
  keep both out. `--reset` clears both lists and plans again. A changed
  severity changes publication, not the evidence or verification of a finding.
  Excluding every finding plans and posts nothing (`NOTHING_TO_POST`).
- **Reopen the saved preview.** `/pr-comment [review-id] --show` displays it
  without a model or Azure DevOps request. It includes the saved adjustments.
- **Read the new preview before publishing.** An adjusted review, including
  one reset since, needs a saved preview planned after its latest adjustment.
  Adjustments are saved together with dropping the earlier preview; a failed
  save changes nothing. A new preview whose save fails is dropped. After a
  stop or restart during planning, prepare a new preview before publishing.
  Once publication starts, the review cannot be adjusted or planned again;
  `--publish` retries the same saved content.
- **Excluded IDs stay out of new comments.** The planner receives the adjusted
  findings, and the assembled preview is checked too. When a retained
  finding's summary names an excluded ID, publication is held until you
  exclude that finding as well or restore the other. References without the
  ID cannot be detected by this check.
- **Earlier PR comments keep their text.** AZPR still skips comments it already
  posted and never edits them. An adjusted review's receipt names items whose
  actual text differs from the preview, including comments that appear only
  when AZPR reads the threads back. It also counts other AZPR comments on the
  PR, where an excluded finding may still be visible.
- The README opens with a real OpenCode 2.1.4 recording of adjusting findings
  and publishing, and the README and quickstart show the adjustment workflow.
  The npm package includes the code of conduct. CI actions are pinned by commit
  and updated with Dependabot.

The options work with review, deep and quick results. Quick findings remain
not independently verified. Without adjustments, comment planning and
publication retain their existing behavior. See the
[commenting guide](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.3.0/docs/COMMENTING.md#adjusting-findings-after-a-preview)
for the complete rules.

## Installation

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.3.0
```

Alternatively, install the same release from Git:

```sh
opencode plugin add 'github:WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2#v0.3.0'
```

Add only one of them. Follow the
[quickstart](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.3.0/docs/QUICKSTART.md)
for a private PAT file, `/pr-setup`, a service restart and the first review.

configuration's `plugins` list:

- For npm, change the package specification to
  `opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.3.0`.
- For Git, change the tag suffix to `#v0.3.0`.

releases.name: v0.2.3 — OpenCode 2.1.4 compatibility
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.2.3

This release moves the tested host to OpenCode CLI 2.1.4 and fixes three
behaviors that OpenCode 2.1.3 and later expose: how a refused proxy tunnel is
reported, how long a silent Azure DevOps call may wait, and how a refused
background summary affects a failed stage. Prompts, settings and installation
are unchanged.

## What changed

- **Proxy refusals are explained again.** OpenCode 2.1.3 and later embed Bun
  1.4.4, which rejects a request with `ERR_PROXY_TUNNEL` when a proxy refuses
  the CONNECT tunnel, where Bun 1.4.2 returned the proxy's answer. AZPR treated
  the rejection as a network error and retried it. It now gives the earlier
  messages and retry rules: a missing proxy password is explained as HTTP 407
  without retries, a blocked destination names the proxy, and a refused tunnel
  never leaves a comment write uncertain.
- **Azure DevOps calls keep their configured timeout.** The runtime's fetch
  ended a request that received nothing for about six minutes by itself, while
  `azure.callTimeoutSeconds` accepts up to 1,800 seconds. AZPR now switches that
  limit off for its requests, so the configured timeout decides.
- **Background compaction no longer splits a failed stage.** With OpenCode's
  opt-in `experimental.background_compaction`, the host asks for a summary
  before a reviewer's context is full. AZPR refuses it as before, but the
  refusal also marked the stage as overflowing: a later permanent failure,
  such as an expired provider key, split the shard into new sessions that
  failed the same way, and a failed follow-up discarded the answer it
  followed. Overflow is now read from the failed turn itself.
- The README states that AZPR is an independent community project, not built
  by or affiliated with the OpenCode team.

## Installation

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.2.3
```

Alternatively, install the same release from Git:

```sh
opencode plugin add 'github:WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2#v0.2.3'
```

Add only one of them. Follow the
[quickstart](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.2.3/docs/QUICKSTART.md)
for a private PAT file, `/pr-setup`, a service restart and the first review.

## Upgrading

Upgrade OpenCode to 2.1.4 first if you can: the receipts of other versions add
a host notice, and those versions are not validated. Stop the OpenCode service
and copy its database before upgrading OpenCode, so that you can go back.

To update a native installation, edit its existing entry in the OpenCode
configuration's `plugins` list:

- For npm, change the package specification to
  `opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.2.3`.
- For Git, change the tag suffix to `#v0.2.3`.

If the entry is an object, change only `package`; preserve `options.settingsFile`
and any other options. Keep one AZPR entry and restart the OpenCode service.
External settings, the PAT file and review records remain in place; a working
configuration needs no new `/pr-setup`. Exact version pins are not advanced by
`opencode plugin update`.

For a source installation, extract the new archive and run its installer with
`--replace` to retain settings:

```sh
sh install.sh --config-dir /absolute/path/to/v2-opencode-config --replace
```

Coming from 0.1.0, see the
[0.2.0 upgrade notes](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.2.0/docs/releases/v0.2.0.md#upgrading-from-010)
for automatic comments, which remain disabled unless configured or requested.

## Compatibility and release assets

The tested target is OpenCode CLI **2.1.4** (V2 plugin API), Node.js
**22.23.3**, Ubuntu **22.04.5** under WSL2, and Azure DevOps Services REST API
**7.1**. OpenCode 1.x and Azure DevOps Server are not supported; other operating
systems remain unvalidated. See the
[validation record](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.2.3/docs/VALIDATION.md),
including live reviews on OpenCode 2.1.4.
